docs.title: We're Mona Lisa Overdrive:
docs.text: A neon heartbeat cracking the room open at the seams with amplifiers singing, all heat and sonic afterburn. There's bands, and then there's Mona Lisa Overdrive. Built on a groove wide enough to sail a battleship through, unbridled elseworlds wails, and supercharger energy, MLO's real show starts when the room begins to shift. When the time seems to curl away somewhere. You may have walked in only breathing. But you're gonna leave living. We're Mona Lisa Overdrive. We'll get you where you're going.

docs.title: Meet the band
docs.text:
"Are you just breathing or you really alive?"

We have but one mission--to make sure that you leave our show in a better state than you arrived.

Little did we know how radical that journey would take us as we started experiencing strange occurrences, strange Mandela effects, blips, and altered history. Then we realized, we'd been harmonizing the strings, different timelines, nullifying the dissonances and crossing over. We had been timeline hopping, and we don't know if we'll ever to get to stop, because so many are chained by the sullen drudgeries of life, and walking through in haze.

We don't know where you need to go, but either way, you're going.

Scott Ewell Twin Turbo Guitar "The sound fell from the sky like a careening star…” Meet one of MLO’s Twin Turbo Guitars, Scott Ewell! Quick to a smile and drawn to unique tones and transitions, Scott complements the gritty fever dream of the overdrive with style and power. Associated Acts Orbital Class Primordial Tides Van Morris Twin Turbo Guitar “It ricocheted in between wavelengths, fusing vibration to electricity…” Equal parts humble artist and backroads rebel, Van's roots are wound tightly with Rock n Roll's own roots. Our other twin turbo guitar weaves the unseen harmonies through each song, gilding them into gold. Associated Acts Honey & Bones The Nobles Van Morris (solo) Jared Bosse Bass Boss “When it awoke, no one knows for sure—but there was no denying its neon heartbeat.” Meet MLO's Bass Boss. A surfer of soundwaves and captivator of cameras, Jared is as hardworking as he is enthusiastic. He seems to run on the very same low end energy he provides, the deep thrum of the overdrive, proving himself a product of his own paradox. Associated Acts Sometimes Fun Loud Music Company Phil Milligan The MF'in Drummer "Or its sudden burst of precise speed, this sentient & liminal supercharger to all who crossed its path.” A master and veteran of his craft, Phil is a musician raised by musicians and spent a decade teaching the next generation hitting the scene now. You would be hard pressed to find someone who can learn the lightning as fast as Phil, or wield its thunder with such precision. Associated Acts Madgallica Hatch Brothers Open Wire Matt Tease The Vox "Light & sound leap & spiral. The ears—they ring, all hallowed howl & elseworlds wail." The swaying, swaggered voice and polychrome maniac of the overdrive. He obsesses over bringing the audience something they’ve never seen, something they can’t forget, and to leave them revitalized. He's also a terrible pool player. Associated Acts Open Wire Still As Wicked

docs.title: About the Band
docs.text:
Named after William Gibson's cyberpunk masterpiece, Mona Lisa Overdrive creates immersive sonic experiences that blur the lines between the nostalgic and the futuristic, the analog and the digital.

Our sound draws from synthwave's retro-futuristic aesthetics, vaporwave's digital dreamscapes, and modern electronic production techniques. Each performance is designed to transport audiences into a neon-lit world where sound, light, and energy converge.

Based in Wilmington, NC, we're not just a band—we're building an entire world. Our approach to live performance goes beyond music, creating complete sensory experiences that engage audiences on multiple levels.

docs.title: Show Dates Template
docs.text: Use this template to add new shows to the show-dates.md file.

docs.title: Adding a New Show
docs.text:
Copy the event card structure below and paste it into the "Upcoming Shows" section of docs/show-dates.md.

Important: Make sure to update the data-date attribute with the correct date in YYYY-MM-DD format. This is what the JavaScript uses to automatically move shows to Past Shows.

<div class="event-card" data-date="YYYY-MM-DD">
<div class="event-date">Month Day, Year</div>
<div class="event-venue">Venue Name w/ Support Acts</div>
<div class="Ticket Price"> ticket or door prive</div>
<div class="Age"> ages allowed</div>
<div class="show time"> when do doors open, when does show start</div>
<div class="event-details">

**SHOW TITLE/THEME** (optional)

Description of the show. What makes this performance special?

**Location:** Venue Name, City, State
**Time:** Door time / Show time
**Tickets:** Link or information
**Special:** Any special notes (guest appearances, themed night, etc.)

Additional details about the show.

</div>
</div>

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<div class="event-card" data-date="2026-05-20">
<div class="event-date">May 20th, 2026</div>
<div class="event-venue">The Observatory w/ Neon Dreams</div>
<div class="event-details">

**OVERDRIVE TOUR**

Join us for an immersive night of synthwave and vaporwave. Full visual production with custom lighting.

**Location:** The Observatory, Charlotte, NC
**Time:** Doors 8pm / Show 9pm
**Tickets:** [Get Tickets](https://ticketlink.com)
**Special:** Limited edition tour merch available

This is one you won't want to miss.

</div>
</div>

docs.title: How the Auto-Move Works
docs.text:
The JavaScript automatically checks show dates: - On page load - At midnight each day

Shows with data-date that have passed will automatically move from "Upcoming Shows" to "Past Shows" (newest first).

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
1. Always use the format data-date="YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g., data-date="2026-12-31")
  2. Keep the event-date display format human-readable (e.g., "December 31st, 2026")
  3. Add new shows to the Upcoming Shows section - the script handles the rest
  4. Past shows are displayed in reverse chronological order (most recent first)

docs.title: DO:
docs.text:
• Use lowercase letters only
  • Use hyphens (-) to separate words
  • Keep ALL original words - do not shorten or abbreviate
  • Be descriptive

docs.title: DON'T:
docs.text:
• Use spaces
  • Use underscores (_)
  • Use capital letters
  • Shorten words

docs.title: Examples:
docs.text:
✓ eagles-dare-debut-show-april-2026.jpg ✓ mona-lisa-overdrive-band-photo-promotional.jpg ✓ behind-the-scenes-sound-check-setup.jpg ✓ front-street-brewery-collaboration-beer.jpg

✗ Eagles Dare Show.jpg (capitals, spaces) ✗ eagles_dare_show.jpg (underscores) ✗ edshow.jpg (shortened/abbreviated) ✗ show1.jpg (not descriptive)

docs.title: Image Quality
docs.text:
• Keep hi-def/full resolution - DO NOT compress or optimize
  • Upload original quality photos
  • Git handles large files fine
  • Only exclude files if they exceed GitHub's 100MB single file limit

docs.title: From photos.md:
docs.text: <img src="images/photos/live/your-photo-name.jpg" alt="Description">

docs.title: From epk.md:
docs.text: <img src="images/epk/your-photo-name.jpg" alt="Description">

docs.title: From any .md file in docs/:
docs.text: All paths are relative to the docs/ folder, so just use images/folder/filename.jpg

docs.title: In photos.md:
docs.text:
1. Upload photo to appropriate folder (live/promo/bts/fan)
  2. Find the relevant section in photos.md
  3. Copy the template card structure (in HTML comments)
  4. Update the src path and alt text
  5. Add caption with event/date info

docs.title: Template:
docs.text:
<div class="card">
<img src="images/photos/live/your-photo-name.jpg" alt="Description" style="width: 100%; border-radius: 8px; margin-bottom: 10px;">
<p style="text-align: center; color: var(--neon-cyan);"><strong>Event Name</strong><br>Date - Venue</p>
</div>

docs.title: Large Files
docs.text:
If you have files larger than 100MB: 1. Consider if they're necessary for web display 2. If needed for archive, store separately 3. Uncomment the exclusion rules in .gitignore 4. Use web-optimized versions for the site (keep originals elsewhere)

Most photos under 10-20MB are fine to commit directly.

docs.title: Hosting Recommendation
docs.text:
DO NOT commit large video files to the repo. Instead:

  1. Upload to YouTube or Vimeo (recommended)
  2. Professional hosting
  3. Bandwidth handling
  4. Better playback experience

  5. Easy embedding

  6. Use embed codes in .md files

  7. YouTube: Get embed code from Share → Embed
  8. Vimeo: Get embed code from Share → Embed

docs.title: Video File Naming (if using local files)
docs.text: Same rules as photos: - Lowercase only - Hyphens instead of spaces - Keep all words - no abbreviations - Examples: ✓ eagles-dare-debut-full-set-april-2026.mp4 ✓ song-title-official-music-video.mp4 ✗ video1.mp4

docs.title: Local Video Files
docs.text:
Only use for: - Small preview clips (under 25MB) - Thumbnails/posters - Short loops/backgrounds

For full videos, always use YouTube/Vimeo embedding.

docs.title: Adding Videos to videos.md
docs.text:
See the HTML comment templates in videos.md for: - YouTube embed structure (responsive) - Vimeo embed structure (responsive) - Local video with controls

Path from videos.md: videos/category/filename.mp4
